# Feature Specification: Public Landing Rebuild + Tools IA + Shared Chrome

**Feature ID**: `003-landing-page`

**Created**: 2026-07-24

**Updated**: 2026-07-24 (greenfield rebuild)

**Status**: Draft — ready for tasks *(prior `tasks.md`, `plan.md`, and `fe-tasks-verify.md` are **stale** relative to this spec and must be regenerated by `@technical-architect`; BA does not rewrite them)*

**Input**: Brand-new public landing (discard old landing visual/structure). Restructure IA for Home, Tools hub, and first nested tool (`/tools/webhooks`). Shared chrome: navigate, login/logout, theme, locale Select with flags. Admin chrome: icon to public home. Research-inspired UX; GSAP scrollytelling remains P1 for the new landing with reduced-motion fallback. Implement features later; Phase 1 structure is routes + chrome + extensible tools shell.

## Clarifications

### Session 2026-07-24 (earlier — retained where still valid)

- `docs/tools` / `docs/langding-page` abandoned — **not revived**.
- Shared extensible tool catalog; FE-first content configuration; English feature docs.
- Reduced-motion accessibility required.
- Placeholder catalog copy OK for P1.

### Session 2026-07-24 (GSAP + `/tools` hub — partially superseded)

- GSAP scrollytelling as P1 motion intent for `/` — **retained** for the **new** landing.
- `/tools` hub + shared catalog — **retained**.
- “Evolve old prototype sections (tokenomics → Tools teaser)” — **superseded** by greenfield rebuild below.
- “Per-tool detail pages are P2 only” — **superseded**: Phase 1 now includes **`/tools/webhooks`** as the first nested tool page (placeholder shell OK; product logic deferred).

### Session 2026-07-24 (greenfield rebuild + shared chrome)

- Q: Evolve vs rebuild landing? → A: **Rebuild.** Discard the old landing approach/structure; new composition may remove retired prototype sections (e.g. tokenomics) entirely. Existing public home route `/` remains the home URL, but the experience is greenfield.
- Q: Current implementation scope? → A: **`/`**, **`/tools`**, **`/tools/webhooks`** only for nested tools in Phase 1. More tools later via catalog + `/tools/{id}` pattern.
- Q: Shared chrome on public marketing/tools surfaces? → A: **Navigate** (Home, Tools, auth destinations); **Login/Logout** (auth-aware); **Theme** (light/dark); **Translate** via **Select with flag icons** for EN and VI — **not** the current EN↔VI toggle button.
- Q: Admin → Home? → A: Admin UI chrome includes an **icon/control that navigates to public home `/`**.
- Q: Locale Select defaults? → A: Select showing **flag + language label**; options **English** and **Tiếng Việt** (EN/VI). Extensible to more locales later without redesign.
- Q: Auth destinations? → A: Reuse existing **`/login`**, **`/register`**, and existing logout behavior.
- Q: Webhooks page content? → A: **Placeholder tool detail shell** with hub-consistent nav and clear path back to `/tools`. Real webhook product logic is out of Phase 1 unless required for page existence.
- Q: Research? → A: Encode technology-agnostic UX patterns from modern marketing + tools-hub sites (see Inspiration Notes). Do not copy brand assets or proprietary copy.

## Inspiration Notes *(research → UX requirements, not brand theft)*

Patterns observed across modern product/marketing and developer-tool sites (e.g. Vercel-style marketing home hierarchy; Linear-style hub card grids into nested pages; SaaS starters with sticky nav + auth + theme + locale; structural-grid landings used by Linear/Vercel/Resend-class sites):

| Pattern | Encode as requirement |
|---------|------------------------|
| Sticky/global header with product nav + CTA/auth | Shared public chrome always reachable |
| First viewport: brand + one headline + support + primary CTA | Hero hierarchy on `/` |
| Hub as card/list entry to nested product pages | `/tools` → `/tools/{id}` |
| Persistent hub/sidebar or back-to-hub on nested pages | Tool pages keep Tools IA chrome |
| Locale switcher as explicit language picker (not cryptic toggle) | Select + flags for EN/VI |
| Theme control adjacent to locale/auth in header | Theme toggle in shared chrome |
| Reduced distraction on conversion surfaces, but multi-page products keep clear nav | Landing may emphasize CTA; still expose Home/Tools/auth |

## Overview

This feature delivers a **greenfield public marketing surface** and an **extensible Tools information architecture**, plus **consistent chrome** across public pages and a **home escape hatch from admin**.

| Route | Role (Phase 1) |
|-------|----------------|
| **`/`** | New scrollytelling landing home (GSAP intent); Tools teaser → hub; shared chrome |
| **`/tools`** | Tools hub — catalog listing with hub chrome |
| **`/tools/webhooks`** | First nested tool page (placeholder shell; proves `/tools/{id}` pattern) |

**Product roadmap / phased delivery**

| Phase | Scope | Status |
|-------|--------|--------|
| **Phase 1 (now)** | New `/` landing; `/tools` hub; `/tools/webhooks` shell; shared public chrome (nav, auth, theme, locale Select+flags); admin → home icon; shared extensible catalog; reduced-motion fallback | **In scope** |
| **Phase 2+** | Additional catalog tools + `/tools/{id}` pages; richer tool apps (real webhooks product); optional hub filters/search; final brand copy | **Deferred** |

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Experience a new scrollytelling home (Priority: P1)

A visitor opens `/` and sees a **new** landing composition (not the retired prototype layout). With motion enabled, scroll-driven section storytelling feels cinematic (GSAP intended). With reduced motion, content remains fully usable.

**Why this priority**: User asked for a brand-new landing with impressive scroll motion.

**Independent Test**: Load `/`; confirm new section structure (no reliance on retired tokenomics prototype); scroll with and without reduced motion.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a visitor on `/` with motion enabled, **When** they scroll, **Then** major sections use scroll-driven transitions (not only static stacks).
2. **Given** reduced-motion preference, **When** viewing `/`, **Then** scrubbed/pinned motion is disabled or simplified and all content/CTAs remain readable and actionable.
3. **Given** Phase 1 ships, **When** stakeholders review `/`, **Then** the page does not depend on the retired prototype section set (e.g. legacy tokenomics) as the primary story.

---

### User Story 2 - Clear first-viewport hierarchy (Priority: P1)

The first viewport communicates brand/product, one primary headline, short support, and at least one primary CTA, consistent with high-performing marketing homes.

**Independent Test**: Open `/` at desktop and 375px width; verify hierarchy without horizontal overflow of primary text/CTAs.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** `/` loads, **When** the first viewport is visible, **Then** brand/product signal, headline, support line, and primary CTA are present.
2. **Given** mobile or desktop, **When** viewing the hero, **Then** primary content remains readable without horizontal page scroll.

---

### User Story 3 - Use shared public chrome: Navigate (Priority: P1)

On public marketing/tools surfaces (`/`, `/tools`, `/tools/webhooks`), a visitor can use clear site navigation to reach Home, Tools, and auth destinations.

**Independent Test**: From each P1 route, use nav links to `/`, `/tools`, `/login` (or register); confirm destinations.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a visitor on any Phase 1 public route, **When** they open site navigation, **Then** they can reach **Home (`/`)** and **Tools (`/tools`)**.
2. **Given** a guest visitor, **When** they use auth navigation, **Then** they can reach **Login** and **Register** (existing routes).
3. **Given** mobile viewport, **When** nav is collapsed (if applicable), **Then** the same destinations remain reachable via an accessible menu.

---

### User Story 4 - Use shared public chrome: Login / Logout (Priority: P1)

Chrome is auth-aware: guests see login/register; signed-in users see logout (and account affordances as appropriate to existing app patterns).

**Independent Test**: Visit `/` as guest and as signed-in user; verify chrome states and logout clears session per existing auth behavior.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a guest on a public P1 route, **When** viewing chrome, **Then** Login and Register entry points are available (Logout is not shown as primary).
2. **Given** a signed-in user on a public P1 route, **When** viewing chrome, **Then** a Logout (or equivalent sign-out) control is available.
3. **Given** a signed-in user, **When** they log out from public chrome, **Then** session ends per existing auth rules and chrome returns to guest state.

---

### User Story 5 - Use shared public chrome: Theme (Priority: P1)

A visitor can switch light/dark (or existing theme modes) from shared chrome; preference persists across `/`, `/tools`, and `/tools/webhooks`.

**Independent Test**: Toggle theme on `/`; navigate to `/tools`; confirm theme persists.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a visitor on a public P1 route, **When** they change theme via chrome, **Then** the surface updates to the selected theme without full loss of place.
2. **Given** a theme preference set on `/`, **When** they open `/tools` or `/tools/webhooks`, **Then** the same theme applies.

---

### User Story 6 - Use shared public chrome: Locale Select with flags (Priority: P1)

A visitor chooses language via a **Select** control showing **flag + language label** for **EN** and **VI**. This replaces the EN↔VI toggle/switch used on prior landing/tools chrome.

**Independent Test**: Open locale Select; choose VI then EN; confirm UI strings update and Select (not toggle) is used on `/`, `/tools`, `/tools/webhooks`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a visitor on a public P1 route, **When** they open the locale control, **Then** it is a **Select** (not a binary toggle button) listing at least English and Vietnamese with flag icons and labels.
2. **Given** the visitor selects Vietnamese, **When** the choice applies, **Then** in-scope UI chrome/copy switches to VI (per existing i18n coverage).
3. **Given** the visitor selects English, **When** the choice applies, **Then** UI returns to EN.
4. **Given** prior EN↔VI toggle UX on landing/tools, **When** Phase 1 ships, **Then** that toggle pattern is no longer the locale control on these surfaces.

---

### User Story 7 - Browse Tools hub and open Webhooks (Priority: P1)

A visitor opens `/tools`, browses the catalog, and opens the Webhooks tool at `/tools/webhooks`. The hub remains the expansion point for future tools.

**Independent Test**: Open `/tools`; confirm Webhooks entry; navigate to `/tools/webhooks`; use back-to-tools.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a visitor on `/tools`, **When** the page loads, **Then** catalog tools are listed (at least Webhooks) with name and short description from the shared catalog.
2. **Given** the Webhooks catalog entry, **When** activated, **Then** the visitor reaches `/tools/webhooks`.
3. **Given** a visitor on `/tools/webhooks`, **When** they use hub/tool chrome, **Then** they can return to `/tools` and to `/` via navigation.

---

### User Story 8 - Webhooks tool page shell (Priority: P1)

`/tools/webhooks` is a real nested tool page: title/identity, placeholder or MVP body, shared/public Tools-aware chrome, and clear “back to Tools”. Full webhook product logic is not required for Phase 1 Done.

**Independent Test**: Direct-load `/tools/webhooks`; confirm shell, chrome, back link; no broken empty route.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a visitor opens `/tools/webhooks` directly, **When** the page loads, **Then** they see a tool page shell identifying Webhooks (not a 404).
2. **Given** the tool page, **When** viewing actions, **Then** a clear path back to `/tools` exists.
3. **Given** Phase 1, **When** reviewing scope, **Then** absence of full webhook runtime features does not fail the page-existence acceptance.

---

### User Story 9 - Landing Tools teaser links to hub (Priority: P1)

The new landing includes a Tools teaser; primary CTA navigates to `/tools`. Optional deep link to `/tools/webhooks` may appear if configured.

**Independent Test**: From `/` Tools section, activate primary CTA → `/tools`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a visitor on `/`, **When** they reach the Tools teaser, **Then** a section landmark and teaser content from the shared catalog are visible.
2. **Given** the Tools teaser primary CTA, **When** activated, **Then** navigation goes to `/tools`.

---

### User Story 10 - Extend catalog without redesign (Priority: P1)

New tools are added via shared catalog entries that can later map to `/tools/{id}` without redesigning hub or landing chrome.

**Independent Test**: Document/config-add a second placeholder tool entry (status coming soon allowed); confirm hub lists it; structure unchanged.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** the shared catalog, **When** a new entry is added with required fields, **Then** `/tools` can list it without redesigning the hub shell.
2. **Given** Webhooks as the first available nested route, **When** future tools ship, **Then** they follow the same `/tools/{id}` IA pattern.
3. **Given** landing teaser and hub, **When** rendering tools, **Then** both draw from the **same** catalog source of truth.

---

### User Story 11 - Admin navigates to public home (Priority: P1)

In the admin UI, a user can activate an icon/control that navigates to the public home `/`.

**Independent Test**: Sign in as admin; from admin chrome, activate home icon; land on `/`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a signed-in user in admin UI, **When** viewing admin header or sidebar chrome, **Then** a home icon/control is present.
2. **Given** that control, **When** activated, **Then** the user navigates to `/`.

---

### User Story 12 - Additional tools and rich tool apps (Priority: P2 — deferred)

More catalog tools, full webhook product features, filters/search, and richer motion on hub pages.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** Phase 1 accepted, **When** adding a new tool, **Then** catalog + `/tools/{id}` + chrome reuse is sufficient without redesigning shared chrome.

---

### Edge Cases

- Reduced motion on `/` → readable static/simplified storytelling.
- Guest vs signed-in chrome → never show contradictory Login + Logout as equal primaries.
- Locale Select keyboard operable; flags have accessible text alternatives (labels, not flag-only).
- Direct load of `/tools/webhooks` without visiting hub first → still usable.
- Coming-soon catalog tools → visible on hub without broken links.
- Theme/locale persistence across public routes; admin theme may follow existing admin patterns but home icon always reaches `/`.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: Product MUST ship a **greenfield** public landing at `/` (retire old landing structure/visual approach as the primary experience).
- **FR-002**: `/` MUST include scroll-driven cinematic section storytelling (GSAP intended) with **reduced-motion fallback**.
- **FR-003**: Phase 1 MUST expose routes **`/`**, **`/tools`**, and **`/tools/webhooks`**.
- **FR-004**: Public P1 routes MUST share chrome for **Navigate**, **Login/Logout**, **Theme**, and **Locale**.
- **FR-005**: Locale control MUST be a **Select** with **flag icons + language labels** for **EN** and **VI**, replacing the EN↔VI toggle on these surfaces.
- **FR-006**: Auth chrome MUST use existing **`/login`**, **`/register`**, and existing logout behavior; guest vs signed-in states MUST differ as specified.
- **FR-007**: Theme control MUST switch light/dark (or existing modes) and persist across public P1 routes.
- **FR-008**: `/tools` MUST list tools from a **shared extensible catalog**.
- **FR-009**: Catalog entries MUST support: `id`, `name`, `description`, `order`, `status`, optional `href` (e.g. `/tools/webhooks`), optional `category`.
- **FR-010**: `/tools/webhooks` MUST exist as a nested tool page shell with back-to-`/tools` and shared chrome; full webhook product logic is not required for P1.
- **FR-011**: Landing Tools teaser MUST primarily navigate to `/tools` and draw from the shared catalog.
- **FR-012**: Admin UI MUST provide an icon/control navigating to public home `/`.
- **FR-013**: UI feature docs remain English; product UI supports EN/VI via i18n.
- **FR-014**: Future tools MUST be addable via catalog + `/tools/{id}` without redesigning hub/landing chrome.

### Key Entities

- **Public chrome**: Shared header/nav controls — Navigate, Auth, Theme, Locale Select.
- **Landing page (`/`)**: New scrollytelling marketing home.
- **Tools hub (`/tools`)**: Catalog listing + hub chrome.
- **Tool page (`/tools/{id}`)**: Nested tool surface; Phase 1 instance = **webhooks**.
- **Tool catalog**: Shared ordered collection driving teaser + hub (+ hrefs to tool pages).
- **Tool entry**: `id`, `name`, `description`, `order`, `status`, optional `href`, optional `category`.
- **Admin home control**: Icon/control in admin chrome linking to `/`.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: Visitor identifies product purpose from `/` hero within 10 seconds.
- **SC-002**: With motion on, reviewer observes scroll-linked transitions across ≥3 major section boundaries on `/`.
- **SC-003**: With reduced motion on, visitor completes hero → mid sections → Tools teaser → CTA with all actions usable.
- **SC-004**: From each of `/`, `/tools`, `/tools/webhooks`, visitor can reach the other two primary destinations via chrome/nav in ≤2 activations.
- **SC-005**: Locale Select (flags + labels) successfully switches EN↔VI on all three P1 routes; old toggle is gone on those surfaces.
- **SC-006**: Guest sees Login/Register; signed-in user can Logout from public chrome (100% in QA matrix).
- **SC-007**: Theme preference set on `/` is still applied on `/tools` after navigation.
- **SC-008**: `/tools/webhooks` loads successfully (not 404) and returns to `/tools` via an explicit control.
- **SC-009**: Admin home icon reaches `/` in one activation.
- **SC-010**: Adding a catalog entry can appear on `/tools` without changing hub page structure.

## Assumptions

- Phase 1 is primarily FE presentation + IA; no CMS required.
- Existing auth feature (`001-auth`) supplies login/register/logout.
- Existing i18n already has EN/VI resources; this feature changes **locale UX control**, not inventing languages.
- Webhooks tool body may be placeholder MVP copy in EN/VI.
- Prior 003 technical artifacts (`tasks.md`, `plan.md`, `fe-tasks-verify.md`) will be **refreshed by `@technical-architect` / implementers** after this spec — treat them as outdated until regenerated.

## Out of Scope (Phase 1)

- Reviving `docs/tools` / `docs/langding-page`.
- Full webhook product/runtime features.
- Additional nested tools beyond webhooks (beyond catalog placeholders marked coming soon).
- Backend CMS.
- New locales beyond EN/VI.
- Keeping the retired landing prototype as the shipped home experience.
